### Code review

Found 2 issues:

1. The new `sql.ErrNoRows` → 404 branch is unreachable and reintroduces a 404 that this handler deliberately no longer has. `GetTripsByIDs` is a sqlc `:many` query (`-- name: GetTripsByIDs :many` in `gtfsdb/query.sql`), so it returns an empty slice with a nil error and never `sql.ErrNoRows` — the PR's own commit message acknowledges this ("since SQL IN queries do not return sql.ErrNoRows naturally"), and the two new tests only reach the branch by injecting `sql.ErrNoRows` through a `tripFetchFailureDB` wrapper into a query that cannot produce it. Commit 3dd2995e removed the identical dead check from this same handler for the same reason, and `trips-for-route` on main now has zero `sendNotFound` calls: "The trips-for-route spec guarantees 200 OK even for unknown routes and out-of-service-area conditions, with no error or 404 case defined." A missing *reference* trip should not turn a successful route response into a 404. The same dead branch is also added at the early-return path (line ~195), where `buildTripReferences` is called with an empty entry list and `nil` prefetched trips and therefore can never fetch anything or error.

https://github.com/OneBusAway/maglev/blob/383fdccc0160c7368194c19cf27d4947479efbe9/internal/restapi/trips_for_route_handler.go#L474-L484

2. The `referencedTripIDs` refactor is behavior-neutral, so the new regression test does not actually cover the reported bug. Every placeholder inserted into `presentTrips` is a bare `models.Trip{}` (lines 539, 550, 559, 570), and those are the only entries with an empty `ID` — prefetched trips come from `gtfsdb.Trip` rows whose `ID` is the primary key. The old `if t.ID == ""` loop therefore selected exactly the same ID set that `referencedTripIDs` now tracks, meaning adjacent block trips were already being fetched. `TestTripsForRouteHandler_BlockSequence_AdjacentTripReferences` would pass against `buildTripReferences` on main unchanged, so it does not demonstrate the empty-object behavior described in #1287. If empty adjacent-trip references are genuinely being observed, the cause is elsewhere and this change won't fix it; worth confirming the failing case reproduces before merging.

https://github.com/OneBusAway/maglev/blob/383fdccc0160c7368194c19cf27d4947479efbe9/internal/restapi/trips_for_route_handler.go#L576-L586

`referencedTripIDs` is redundant given the dedup check already in place. All four insertion sites (lines ~734-737, ~745-748, ~754-757, ~765-768) are already gated by `if _, exists := presentTrips[id]; !exists { ... }` - that guard *is* "not yet fetched." `tripIDsToFetch` could be appended to directly inside each of those guards (`tripIDsToFetch = append(tripIDsToFetch, id)`), which would drop this map plus the second loop here (lines 773-776) entirely, while keeping the same explicit-tracking intent the PR is going for - just without the extra map that has to be kept in sync by convention across four call sites.

Replacing the `t.ID == ""` zero-value heuristic with an explicit set of referenced trip IDs is a readability win — encoding "which trips do we still need to fetch" as an actual set rather than inferring it from a sentinel is the better expression of the intent. The `DBTX` wrapper for forcing lookup failures is a nice testing technique too.

Two things are blocking, though.

**1. The refactor is behavior-neutral, so it doesn't fix #1287.** Placeholders are always bare `models.Trip{}`, and prefetched trips always carry a non-empty primary-key ID, so the old `t.ID == ""` loop selected exactly the same set that `referencedTripIDs` now tracks. `TestTripsForRouteHandler_BlockSequence_AdjacentTripReferences` would pass against the current `buildTripReferences` on `main` unchanged. Whatever is actually causing the empty adjacent-trip references in #1287, this isn't it — so there's a reproducing case still to find before a fix is worth landing.

**2. The `sql.ErrNoRows` → 404 branch is dead, and reintroduces something deliberately removed.** `GetTripsByIDs` is a sqlc `:many` query, so it never returns `ErrNoRows` — the 404 tests only reach that branch through an injected error the DB layer can't produce. More to the point, `3dd2995e` removed the identical dead check from this same handler on the grounds that the trips-for-route spec defines no 404 case, and `main`'s handler has no `sendNotFound` at all: even a missing agency returns an empty 200 list (`trips_for_route_handler.go:39-45`). A reference-lookup failure shouldn't be the thing that reintroduces a 404 here.

Related and worth deciding deliberately rather than by default: escalating a `buildTripReferences` DB failure to a 500 also reverses this handler's posture. `main` logs and continues when reference resolution fails, and `3dd2995e` argues explicitly that a per-entry resolution failure shouldn't fail the whole response. CONTRIBUTING's non-`ErrNoRows` → 500 rule does cut the other way, so I don't think you were wrong to reach for it — but this handler has an established answer and it's the other one.

The branch also conflicts with `main` now; `buildTripReferences` has gained a `stopIDMap` parameter since you cut it.

If you can get a reproducing case for #1287 I'm very interested — the underlying report may well be real even though this change doesn't move it.

## Two-stage review (spec conformance + code quality)

**Spec conformance:** Verified this refactor is behavior-neutral. I traced all
four `referencedTripIDs` insertion sites (`preFetchedTrips` loop, entry
`TripId` loop, `schedule.previousTripId`/`nextTripId` loop, `status.activeTripId`
loop) against the old `t.ID == ""` heuristic they replace - in every case,
including IDs referenced from multiple places, the new set-based fetch list is
identical to the old one. No new spec deviation is introduced by this PR, and
the new tests are solid regression coverage for the existing (unchanged)
reference-resolution behavior.

Reviewing this did surface a pre-existing, previously undocumented deviation
in this handler: when a referenced-trip/route DB lookup inside
`buildTripReferences` fails, Maglev logs and returns `200 OK` with that
reference silently dropped, whereas Java's `TripsForRouteAction.show()` only
catches `OutOfServiceAreaServiceException` and lets any other exception
propagate to a `500`. This predates #1288 (it's the posture `3dd2995e`
deliberately established) and isn't something to change in this PR - it's now
recorded in `maglev.wiki`'s Implementation Decisions for `trips-for-route`, no
action needed here.

**Code quality:** two small items below - a simplification and a commit-message
nit. Neither is functionally broken, so not blocking, but worth tightening
before merge.

---

Two things noticed while reading the surrounding code that are **out of scope
for this PR** (different handler / pre-existing lines untouched by this diff),
flagging only so they don't get lost:

- `trips_for_route_handler.go:883` - `if route, ok := presentRoutes[trip.RouteID]; ok`
  checks map-key presence, not whether the route was actually resolved. A
  placeholder route key is inserted before `GetRoutesByIDs` fills it in, so if
  that batched fetch fails, the trip is still emitted with an empty
  `AgencyID`, producing a malformed combined ID (e.g. `"_1234"`). Pre-existing,
  untouched by this diff - probably worth its own issue.
- `trip_details_handler.go`'s `buildReferencedTrips` has the same
  drop-on-not-found pattern for a trip referenced by `status.ActiveTripID`,
  which can legitimately miss for DUPLICATED GTFS-RT trips with synthetic IDs
  (per `trips_helper.go`'s own comments). That feeds into an iOS force-unwrap
  (`OBAKitCore/Models/REST/TripStatus.swift:198`) on endpoints iOS calls
  constantly - looks like a real crash risk, unrelated to this PR, worth its
  own issue.
